audit_scope.description: This batch covers EL state transitions (EIP-158 empty account clearing, Frontier block processing, Tangerine Whistle gas repricing, EIP-1344 CHAINID), EL networking (EIP-706 Snappy compression, EIP-2976 typed transactions), EL JSON-RPC interfaces (EIP-3041 block queries, EIP-3046 uncle queries, EIP-3326 chain switching), and the EL-CL interface (EIP-3675 PoW to PoS merge transition).

in_scope: State Transition (empty account clearing, gas repricing, CHAINID opcode)
Block Processing (Frontier block validation, post-merge validation)
P2P Networking (DEVp2p Snappy compression, block propagation)
Engine API (fork choice updates from CL)
Engine API interface to EL (fork choice updates, execution payload proposals)
out_of_scope: Beacon chain internal logic (attestations, validator management)

misclassified_entities.reason: Internal EL component. The EVM interpreter is part of the execution layer, not an external entity. It executes within the system boundary.
Internal EL component. Smart contracts executing CALL opcodes are running within the EVM, inside the system boundary.
Internal EL component. Contract bytecode executing SELFDESTRUCT runs within the EVM, inside the system boundary.
Internal EL component. EVM SLOAD/SSTORE operations are internal state trie operations within the execution layer.
Internal EL component. The eth/les subprotocol is part of the node's networking stack, not an external entity.

trusted_external_entities.name: User/DApp via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated public RPC interface. Any user, DApp, or attacker can submit requests. Covers EIP-3041 block queries, EIP-3046 uncle queries, EIP-3326 chain switch requests, and general transaction submission. All input must be fully validated.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node via P2P Network (devp2p)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P Network (devp2p Hello handshake, Transactions/NewBlock/NewBlockHashes/BlockBodies messages, Snappy compressed payloads)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated P2P network peers. Any node can connect and send messages. Covers EIP-706 Snappy compression, EIP-2976 typed transaction gossip, Frontier block propagation, and EIP-3675 pre-finalization block gossip. Malicious peers may send decompression bombs, unknown transaction types, or invalid blocks. All data must be validated.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Sender via Signed Transaction
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Transaction submission (signed transactions entering block processing pipeline)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External accounts submitting signed transactions. While ECDSA signatures authenticate the sender, the transaction content (value, data, gas) is fully attacker-controlled. Covers EIP-158 touch triggers, Frontier transaction execution, and EIP-1344 cross-chain replay scenarios. Full transaction validation required.

trusted_external_entities.name: Consensus Layer via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Authenticated via JWT shared secret between EL and CL clients. The CL provides fork choice updates (head, safe, finalized block hashes) and execution payloads after the merge (EIP-3675). While the channel is authenticated, execution payload content must still be validated (block header fields, state roots, deprecated PoW fields must be zero).

trusted_external_entities.name: PoW Miner via P2P Network
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P Network (mined block submission during pre-merge PoW phase)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Miners submit blocks via the P2P network during the pre-merge era. Blocks must be fully validated including PoW proof, difficulty, and total difficulty calculations. An attacker could attempt to trigger the merge transition on a minority fork by manipulating total difficulty (EIP-3675).

trusted_external_entities.name: Malicious Peer via Crafted Compressed Payload
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P Network (DEVp2p v5 Snappy compressed messages)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Attacker sending crafted Snappy payloads to exploit decompression. EIP-706 specifically addresses decompression bombs (>16MB), varint overflow attacks, and corrupted compressed data. Pre-decompression size validation is critical.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Block hash and uncle index parameters must be validated. Response must correctly include/exclude baseFee field based on EIP-1559 fork status. No authentication required for read-only queries, but rate limiting should be applied.

Chain ID must be validated as proper hex format (EIP-695). Wallet must verify chain is known and serviceable. User confirmation required before switching. Privacy risk: automatic rejection of unknown chains may leak wallet capabilities enabling fingerprinting attacks.
Protocol version must be negotiated correctly. Compression is enabled only after both peers agree on DEVp2p v5+. Version mismatch must not cause undefined behavior.

Decompressed message size must be validated against 16MB limit BEFORE decompression. Snappy varint must be validated (<= 2^32-1). Corrupted compressed data must be handled gracefully (reject message, potentially disconnect peer).

TransactionType byte must be in valid range (0-0x7f). Unknown transaction types SHOULD trigger peer disconnection. Transaction payloads must be validated per type-specific rules. Pre-fork-activation transactions of new types MUST be rejected.

Full block validation required: header fields, transaction signatures, nonce sequence, balance checks, state root verification. Invalid blocks must be rejected. After merge, blocks containing unknown transaction types in their body must be rejected entirely.

ECDSA signature validation, nonce check, balance sufficiency check, gas limit validation. EIP-158: account touches from zero-value operations must correctly trigger emptiness evaluation. EIP-1344: CHAINID opcode must return consistent chain ID matching EIP-155 transaction signing to prevent cross-chain replay.

JWT authentication validates channel. Execution payload content must still be validated: post-merge blocks must have difficulty=0, nonce=0, empty ommers, mixHash=0 (EIP-3675). State root must be verified after transaction execution. Invalid deprecated field values must cause block rejection.

JWT authentication validates channel. Head, safe, and finalized block hashes must reference known blocks. Finalized block must be an ancestor of the head block. After first finalization, block gossip messages (NewBlock, NewBlockHashes) are deprecated and must be ignored.

PoW proof must be validated. Total difficulty computation must be accurate to correctly identify the terminal block for the merge transition (EIP-3675). An attacker accumulating hash power on a minority fork to reach TTD first must not be able to hijack the transition.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: DEVp2p v5 Snappy compressed message receive
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Decompression bomb protection: validate decompressed size via Snappy varint header before allocating memory. Varint overflow check (must be <= 2^32-1). Size must be <= 16MB (DEVp2p message limit). Snappy library must be free of buffer overflow vulnerabilities. Memory exhaustion from concurrent large messages must be mitigated.
